chunks.text: Today we cover interferometric synthetic aperture radar. InSAR measures ground displacement by comparing the phase of two radar acquisitions over the same area.

Persistent scatterer techniques, often called PSInSAR, track stable reflectors such as buildings across hundreds of Sentinel-1 scenes. Older missions like ALOS and Envisat extend the record back in time.
Satellite observations need ground truth. We tie the interferogram to GNSS stations and to leveling surveys so the geodetic reference frame is consistent.
Airborne lidar adds high resolution elevation models, which help separate natural compaction of deltaic sediment from subsidence caused by pumping.

Finally, machine learning is increasingly used here. A convolutional neural network can flag unwrapping errors, and an LSTM can forecast displacement time series, but a physics-based numerical model is still needed to interpret the causes.
